To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the standard LZ factorization can be computed in Θ(n)-time and linear space using a suffix array and (2) the enhanced suffix array can be computed in O(n) expected time and linear space using the same data structures as those needed for LZ factorization.
the following algorithms are optimal in the worst case: (i) a true Θ(n)-space LZx algorithm, (ii) an O(n)-time LZx algorithm, and (iii) a Θ(n)-time LZ factorization algorithm.

(a) the Lempel-Ziv factorization of a string can be computed in O(n) time and space, and (b) the Lempelian factorization of a text can be computed in time and space linear in the length of the text, without any preprocessing.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) the design and implementation of new suffix array based LZ factorization algorithms; (ii) the analysis of the space and time complexity of these algorithms; (iii) the implementation of these algorithms; and (iv) the empirical evaluation of these algorithms.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the worst case, the suffix array-based algorithms are the fastest known algorithms for Lempel– Ziv factorization, and that, in practice, the suffix array algorithms are often faster than the suffix tree algorithm, especially for large alphabets.

our algorithms are superior to the previous ones in the following respects: they are faster (sometimes by a factor of 2), they are more space-efficient (by a factor of 3 to 10) and they are more flexible in the choice of the underlying data structure.
, for the most important practical applications, our methods are the best known for LZ factorization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a way to do LZx in time Θ(n) and space O(n) using only a suffix array.
the suffix array is a more flexible data structure than the suffix tree, and that in many practical circumstances it is the best choice for LZ factorization.

, for a given input x, the suffix tree ST(x), the suffix array SA(x), the enhanced suffix array ESA(x) of Abouelhida et al., and our suffix array SA(x) are all equivalent in that they all yield the same Lempel– Ziv factorization of x; however, in terms of worst-case space complexity and/or time complexity, SA(x) is clearly the best of the four.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, contrary to the conventional wisdom, it is indeed possible to compute LZ factorization of a string in time linear in the length of the string, using space linear in the alphabet size, without the need for tree data structures.
, for LZ factorization and related tasks, the suffix array is a more natural data structure than the suffix tree, and it is also more space-efficient.
suffix array-based algorithms for LZ factorizations can be much more space- and time-efficient than those based on suffix trees.
